name: Medical image segmentation

conventions.text: Bracket the network with the scan and its segmentation: a real image slice at the input and the predicted mask at the output (colour-coded labels overlaid on the slice, or a binary mask).
For volumetric data, draw the scan in perspective: a tilted slice plane, or a cube with an axial slice on its front face.
Stand the U upright: the encoder descends the left side, the decoder climbs back up the right, and input and output sit at the top.
Label each level by its size as a fraction of the input (H/4 x W/4 ... H/16 x W/16, or 1/4, 1/8, 1/16) beside the stage or on its skip or fusion arrow.
When CNN and Transformer parts are combined, give each family its own colour: warm yellow or orange for the Transformer side against grey or green for the CNN side.
Wrap each part of the network (encoder, transformer or bottleneck, decoder) in its own dashed rounded container named by its role.
Repeat the proposed block as an identical box at every level where it occurs, and expand only one copy (the topmost) into a detail panel.
Tie a detail panel to its source box with thin zoom lines or a translucent wedge fanning out from the small box.
Mix 3-D cuboids for feature maps or resampling operations with flat boxes for the named blocks.

source: summarised from the evidence cards listed under each convention
